result.title: Transfer Once, Ask Locally: Compact Audio-Visual Memory for On-Device Question Answering
result.summary: Audio-visual question answering on lightweight user devices requires balancing speed, memory usage, privacy, and communication. One approach is to run audio-visual encoders on a server and a lightweight language decoder on the user device, keeping questions local while offloading media encoding. However, transferring and processing the full multimodal representation remains costly. We propose a training-free, query-agnostic token pruning framework that constructs a compact, reusable memory before transmission. We define video spatio-temporal blocks and aligned audio windows as players and estimate their importance through Monte Carlo Shapley valuation. We use an embedding coverage objective that combines query-independent utility with cross-modal redundancy calibration and rewards unimodal diversity through marginal coverage gains. We retain the original token embeddings of high-scoring players under a limited token budget and transfer the resulting memory once for reuse across subsequent local questions. Experiments on Video-MME, Daily-Omni, and Video-Holmes using video-SALMONN 2+ (3B) and video-SALMONN 2 Pro (4B) show that our method achieves the best or tied-best QA accuracy among the compared compression methods across all evaluated settings. On Daily-Omni with video-SALMONN 2+ (3B) at 80\% pruning, our method improves accuracy by 12.86--14.62 percentage points over these methods while achieving the lowest device-side LLM prefill and decoding latency, with up to $1.92\times$ decoding speedup at comparable embedding memory usage.

AI.brief_summary: 该论文提出一种免训练、与查询无关的音视频 token 剪枝框架：以时空块与音频窗为单位，用 Monte Carlo Shapley 估值并配合嵌入覆盖目标筛选 token，在预算内构造可复用的紧凑多模态记忆以降低传输与端侧开销。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「用重要性估值加覆盖目标在有限预算下挑选可复用多模态记忆」的做法，可为 LVR 中视觉证据筛选、贡献分配与 latent 预算/缓存设计提供可核查线索，但论文本身面向压缩与端侧效率，未涉及推理期 latent 状态生成与使用。
